text:
Vladislav Gavrikov plays 21 and a half minutes a night beside Adam Fox on the Rangers' top pair, and he has one point in his last ten games. That's not really the job, though. He's there to make the pair responsible, and the Rangers take about 53% of the expected goals with him on the ice.

The shooting has been cold: one goal on a 3.6% shooting percentage, half of what defensemen usually see. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level, but noted he was better than his goals, with the chances there and the finishing or goaltending behind him not. With Sean Durzi out, he matters more.

And for something different: Mollie Walker of the New York Post wrote about his appearance on an adventure game show in Russia that he watched every weekend growing up. Our range has him at 23 to 41 points over a full season, which depends a lot on whether the puck starts going in for the Rangers' top unit. A sixth-round pick in 2015, he has turned into a dependable top-pair defenseman.
headline: Gavrikov, the quiet half of the top pair
